headline: High: AutoGen’s default code-execution and filesystem access can conflict with Pathway’s document-processing flow, creating medium-to-high risks of leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write working directories and execute tool calls; Pathway is a document-processing system, so if Pathway outputs are fed into AutoGen as files or text, instruction-like content could be treated as trusted input. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are copied into AutoGen prompts or shared files without provenance tags, injection risk exists.
IF AutoGen agents parse document text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/provenance header to all Pathway outputs before AutoGen reads them.
Disable automatic tool execution on untrusted document text.
Route Pathway outputs through a human review step before prompting AutoGen.
Use separate directories for Pathway inputs and AutoGen working files.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys, and it has broad network egress plus filesystem access. Pathway is document-processing, so if both share a workspace, AutoGen can read and transmit document contents to configured model providers. Pathway itself has no network or file access, so the leakage path is one-way through AutoGen.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or working directory, AutoGen can read Pathway-produced documents.
IF AutoGen forwards those documents to model providers, document contents leave the local environment.
mitigations: Place Pathway and AutoGen in separate directories with OS permissions.
Disable AutoGen access to sensitive folders.
Redact or tokenize documents before AutoGen ingestion.
Use a local-only model backend for AutoGen where possible.
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls and egress policy enforcement.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Pathway is a document-processing system with no write or shell capability. If they operate on the same workspace, AutoGen can overwrite or race on shared artifacts even though Pathway itself cannot modify them. The conflict is plausible from the profiles, but shared-write overlap is not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same output directory, AutoGen can overwrite Pathway artifacts.
IF the orchestrator lacks locking, concurrent runs can corrupt shared files.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories to each agent.
Turn off AutoGen write access unless needed.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Keep Pathway outputs immutable once produced.
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen’s multi-agent orchestration can consume upstream outputs as inputs, and Pathway produces document-processing results that may be treated as authoritative. If Pathway emits incorrect or incomplete data, AutoGen may propagate it into downstream actions or code execution without verification. The pairwise chain is inferred, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF AutoGen uses Pathway outputs as prompts or task inputs without validation, errors can cascade.
IF downstream AutoGen agents take actions based on Pathway-derived facts, mistakes become operational.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Pathway and AutoGen.
Require citations or source links for any Pathway-derived claim.
Flag low-confidence Pathway outputs for review.
Limit AutoGen actions to read-only until validation passes.
requires-engineering: add schema checks and provenance tracking.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but only AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and application data; Pathway’s profile shows no data classes or residency claims. No concrete residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to configuration-dependent handling rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF sensitive data is routed through AutoGen to a non-compliant model provider, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF Pathway processes regulated data and the deployment lacks a DPA or retention controls, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Confirm the model provider’s compliance terms before use.
Avoid sending regulated data through AutoGen.
Document retention and deletion settings for both systems.
Keep Pathway outputs de-identified where possible.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
